what: A design system is a shared set of design tokens (named colours, sizes, spacing), reusable accessible components and usage guidance that every product team builds from. Tokens feed the components, themes swap token values, and a tool like Storybook documents and tests each component in isolation.
like: Like a LEGO set with an instruction booklet: everyone uses the same bricks, so whatever different people build still looks and fits together.
why: Consistent look and behaviour across screens and teams
Faster delivery: teams reuse components instead of rebuilding buttons
Accessibility and brand fixes made once reach every product

steps.d: Tokens are named design decisions stored as data. The W3C Design Tokens Community Group format uses JSON with $value, optional $type and aliases like {colour.brand}.
A build step turns tokens into CSS custom properties (and native formats if needed). Themes, such as dark mode, redefine the same variable names with different values.
Components read var(--color-...) instead of hard-coded values, include keyboard, focus and ARIA behaviour, and expose a small, stable API.
Storybook renders each state as a story, generates docs, and supports interaction, accessibility and visual tests so changes are caught before release.
The library is published as a versioned package. Apps upgrade deliberately, with semantic versioning and a changelog, so a change in one place does not surprise every team.

numbers.l: minimum contrast for normal text under WCAG 2.2 level AA; 3:1 for large text
what counts as large text (about 24 px and 18.5 px) for the lower 3:1 ratio
latest published version of the Design Tokens Format Module - still a Community Group draft, not a W3C Standard

choices.d: Start from an accessible headless or open-source base and add your tokens and styling, rather than writing focus management and ARIA for dialogs and menus from scratch.
Use primitive tokens (blue-500), semantic tokens (color-action) and component tokens. Components should only use semantic ones, which makes theming a re-mapping job.
CSS custom properties work with any framework and update at runtime for themes. They are inherited, and can be redefined under prefers-color-scheme or a data-theme attribute.
Versioned npm package with a changelog and codemods for breaking changes. Add 'use client' to entry points that need it so the library works in Server Components.

instead.why: Accessibility rules the components must satisfy
How separate teams share one UI kit without sharing a deploy

breaks.d: Every change needs the core team and releases are slow.
breaks.see: Teams fork components or copy styles
breaks.fix: Contribution model, clear ownership, slots and composition so teams extend instead of fork

breaks.d: A dark theme or brand colour fails contrast.
breaks.fix: Check semantic token pairs against 4.5:1 and 3:1 in CI, with automated a11y tests in Storybook

breaks.d: A prop rename ships in a minor version.
breaks.see: Multiple products fail after bumping the package
breaks.fix: Semantic versioning, deprecation period, codemods, visual regression tests

say: I would build the design system in layers: tokens as the single source of truth, components that consume only semantic tokens, and Storybook for docs and tests.
Theming is just redefining the CSS custom properties, so dark mode and brands don't need component changes, and I check text contrast pairs against 4.5 to 1.
It ships as a versioned package with a changelog, and I measure adoption and a11y test results so the system earns trust and does not become a bottleneck.

followups.q: Where do design tokens come from and go to?
followups.a: Designers define them in a tool or a tokens JSON file; a build step transforms them into CSS variables and other platform formats. The Design Tokens Community Group format is the emerging interchange standard.

followups.q: How do you keep many products on the latest version?
followups.a: Semantic versioning, a published roadmap and deprecations, codemods for breaking changes, and automated visual and accessibility tests so upgrades are low risk.

today: The W3C Design Tokens Community Group published Format Module 2025.10 as a draft interchange format, and Storybook is commonly used with interaction, accessibility and visual tests as the quality gate for component libraries.

check.why: 3:1 applies to large text; 7:1 is the AAA level.
